ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this case goes to a human reviewer. The disputed $6.00 cancellation fee stays on hold — neither collected from you nor refunded — until that review is decided. That is already the state of the fare record, whose payment_status is PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

WHY IT ESCALATES. POL-NS-09(c) makes escalation mandatory where the same rider and the same driver have 2 or more no-show disputes in the trailing 90 days. Both profiles carry that figure: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2 (EV-RPROF-00213 and EV-DPROF-00213, each weight 1.0), which matches the rider's own words, 'same driver as the last two times'. Escalation is TERMINAL: it replaces any monetary ruling, so I issue no refund and no compensation. Both advocates agree this trigger is engaged.

WHY THE FEE ITSELF CANNOT BE DECIDED HERE. The two instruments that would decide it are absent. The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00213, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and the chat log (EV-CHAT-00213, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) are not in the platform's pipeline. Those are the artifacts that settle whether the driver was inside the 150 m TRANSPORT_HUB arrival radius (POL-NS-02) and whether he held the free waiting period measured from GPS entry (POL-NS-01(c)). Without them those limbs are UNDECIDED — not failed, and not satisfied.

DRIVER'S POINTS. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00213, weight 1.0) is complete and does show an 'arrived' event at 17:47:05 and a driver cancellation at 17:53:40, a 395-second interval, with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_UNREACHABLE — one of the codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, so limb (d) is met. But POL-NS-01(c) runs the dwell clock from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap, and trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is BUTTON, so POL-NS-12's platform-confirmed (GPS_AUTO) shortcut is unavailable. The 395 seconds therefore cannot establish the required 300-second free-wait dwell, and the $4.80 payout the money block computes at 80% of $6.00 is not reached. The anti-farming check does NOT trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3, below the count of 4, and 3 of 107 completed trips is 2.8%, below the 8% rate — so no compensation is withheld on that ground and no refund is directed into any packet. The claim mentioning prior_no_show_flags is noted only to record that that lifetime counter is NOT the field POL-NS-07 reads; it was used for nothing.

RIDER'S POINTS. A missing trace is not a trace showing the driver outside the radius: POL-NS-02's proviso addresses a sparse trace, whereas a missing artifact carries no fact at all, so limb (b) is undecided rather than failed and no full refund follows. POL-NS-05's false-arrival referral is likewise not established, because testing whether the 17:47:05 button tap was false needs a GPS fix and there is none; that question stays open for the reviewer and is not a clause-mandated referral. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider because its limbs (a) and (b) both read the chat log, which is absent — but the loss is not held against her: trip_record.chat_message_count of 3 shows a log existed, making the chat log impaired under POL-NS-08(c), and the driver's assertion that he answered every message is equally unverifiable. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00213-01, weight 0.0) removes POL-NS-06 limb (i)'s dwell accumulation from the driver's side as well.

WHAT I ACCEPT. The fare line reconciles: the $6.00 cancellation_fee equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged and no refund follows from the arithmetic.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE REVIEWER. (1) Was the driver inside the 150 m arrival radius, and did he hold 300 seconds measured from GPS entry (POL-NS-02, POL-NS-01(c))? (2) Did he reply within 120 seconds, or make an in-app call (POL-NS-04(b))? (3) Was the BUTTON arrival marker false (POL-NS-05)? These cannot be answered on the present record, which is why the fee is held rather than decided.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
